Mom's Mexican Chicken (Jennifer Sue Jacks Henley)

My mom passed in 2011 and this recipe is one of the many fond memories I have of her and the good times our family shared. The picture itself is not mine, I grabbed it off of the internet, I just tried to find one that kind of looks like her's normally did. The picture is kind of like what the chicken looked like before it was placed on the corn tortillas.

****Servings: ****

  • 4 to 6 Chicken Breasts
  • 1 Medium Onion
  • 2 Whole Jalapenos
  • 1/2 Stick of Butter
  • 1 Can Cream Of Chicken Soup
  • 3/4 a Can Of Chicken Stalk (Mom used the stalk she got from boiling the breasts)
  • 3/4 package of cheddar cheese
  • 12 Corn Tortillas

Directions

  • Boil chicken (4 to 6 breasts)
  • While chicken is cooking, saute 1 medium onion and 2 Jalapenos in 1/2 stick of butter.
  • Add cream of chicken soup with the 3/4 a can of chicken stock. Blend well.
  • Shred and add the cooked chicken to the mixture.
  • In a large casserole dish, Place a row of tortillas to line the bottom.
  • Place mix that was just made on top of the tortillas.
  • Cover with another row of tortillas, Repeat until gone.
  • Top with one package of cheddar cheese.
  • Heat in the oven for about 20 minutes at 350

Side note, she also sometimes added one can of Ro*tel Tomato's to what she cooked, but it is not in her "official" recipe.

Another variation that my mother would never do, but we did when we would make it at my house was to mix the items together and set the mix on the table when hot and just add it to warm corn or flour tortillas at the table.

Last of all if you are low on cash, try substituting a whole chicken for the chicken breasts, it will produce a better chicken stalk, and normally the meat is cheaper that way. Just boil the whole chicken like people normally do for chicken soup. (reference link) http://allrecipes.com/recipe/homemade-chicken-soup/
